rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the two arguments entail expiation when a person breaks an oath expressed as ‘No, by God; yes, by God.’
rows.anchor: فهاتان الحجتان يوجبان الكفارة في قول الناس : لا والله بلى والله ، إذا حصل الحنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic yamin means strength; the cited poetic line uses the word in that sense.
rows.anchor: أن اليمين في اللغة عبارة عن القوة قال الشاعر :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi favors Abu Hanifa’s account over al-Shafi‘i’s: an oath about the past is laghw because it cannot strengthen resolve about a future act.
rows.anchor: ويجب تفسيره بما قاله أبو حنيفة أن اليمين في اللغة عبارة عن القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view calls an oath to abandon obedience or commit sin laghw, treating the sin itself as the idle matter.
rows.anchor: إذا حلف على ترك طاعة ، أو فعل معصية ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That view links laghw to turning away from idle speech and reads earning by the heart as persisting in the sworn disobedience.
rows.anchor: أي بإقامتكم على ذلك الذي حلفتم عليه من ترك الطاعة وفعل المعصية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says that one who swears an oath and then sees a better course should do what is better and expiate the oath.
rows.anchor: من حلف على يمين فرأى غيرها خيرا منها فليأت الذي هو خير ثم ليكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the third view: al-Ma’idah 5:89 identifies accountability with expiation, and earning by the heart suggests a new act rather than persistence.
rows.anchor: المؤاخذة المذكورة في هذه الآية صارت مفسرة في آية المائدة بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the expiated oath is called laghw because expiation removes its sin, so God does not hold the person to account once it is expiated.
rows.anchor: أنها اليمين المكفرة سميت لغوا لأن الكفارة أسقطت الإثم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi interprets laghw as an accidental, unintended utterance, since the verse contrasts it with what hearts deliberately earn.
rows.anchor: أن المراد به ما يقع سهوا غير مقصود إليه

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi‘i argues that combining this verse’s heart-binding language with al-Ma’idah 5:89 makes expiation due for every serious oath, including a false oath sworn knowingly.
rows.anchor: كل يمين ذكر على سبيل الجد وربط القلب ، فالكفارة واجبة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghafūr emphatically covers sins and removes their punishment.
rows.anchor: الغفور ، مبالغة في ستر الذنوب ، وفي إسقاط عقوبتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥalīm means God does not hasten punishment but delays punishment of unbelievers and evildoers; the Arabic root conveys calm patience.
rows.anchor: في صفة الله : الذي لا يعجل بالعقوبة ، بل يؤخر عقوبة الكفار والفجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi gives two readings of repentance: abandoning usurious dealings, or abandoning the belief that usury is lawful.
rows.anchor: على القول الأول تبتم من معاملة الربا / وعلى القول الثاني من استحلال الربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Receiving only the principal prevents injustice in both directions: the creditor may not demand an increase, and the debtor may not be deprived of principal.
rows.anchor: لا تظلمون الغريم بطلب الزيادة على رأس المال ، ولا تظلمون أي بنقصان رأس المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians use kāna either as a complete verb meaning occurred or existed, with no predicate, or as a defective verb that needs a predicate.
rows.anchor: أن تكون بمنزلة حدث ووقع ، وذلك في قوله : قد كان الأمر ، أي وجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its defective use, kāna sheds the separate event meaning and marks time, so it requires a predicate, as in ‘Zayd was going.’
rows.anchor: أن يخلع منه معنى الحدث ، فتبقى الكلمة مجردة للزمان ، وحينئذ يحتاج إلى الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Khwarazm, Razi challenged leading litterateurs: if kāna is a verb it must be complete, while if incomplete it would have to be a particle, contrary to their view.
rows.anchor: إنكم تقولون إن { كان } إذا كانت ناقصة إنها تكون فعلا وهذا محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says kāna means an event or occurrence in both uses: a complete verb marks an entity’s occurrence, while a defective one marks the occurrence of a subject’s being described by a predicate.
rows.anchor: المفهوم من { كان } في الموضعين هو الحدوث والوقوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna can mean ‘became’; an anonymous poetic line about birds and their eggs illustrates this sense.
rows.anchor: بتيهاء قفر والمطي كأنها قطا الحزن قد كانت فراخا بيوضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi explains ‘became’ as a new occurrence in which a subject acquires a description it did not previously have.
rows.anchor: حدث موصوفية الذات بهذه الصفة بعد أنها ما كانت موصوفة بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians also treat kāna as redundant, citing an anonymous line about fine horses.
rows.anchor: سراة بني أبي بكر تسامى على كان المسومة الجياد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reads kāna here as a complete verb meaning ‘occurred’: whenever anyone is in hardship, that person receives respite; reading it as ‘if the buyer is insolvent’ would wrongly narrow the rule.
rows.anchor: أنها بمعنى وقع وحدث ، والمعنى : وإن وجد ذو عسرة

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: An alternative parses kāna as defective with an omitted predicate, ‘a debtor to you’; Uthman’s accusative reading and another reported reading make the debtor explicit.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عثمان { ذا * عسرة } والتقدير : إن كان الغريم ذا عسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿUsra is inability to find available money, the condition in which money is hard to obtain.
rows.anchor: العسرة اسم من الأعسار ، وهو تعذر الموجود من المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause omits its subject or predicate: the implied meaning is that the ruling, command, or person you deal with is respite.
rows.anchor: في الآية حذف ، والتقدير : فالحكم أو فالأمر نظرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naẓira means delay or granting respite, as in the request to be kept waiting until the appointed time.
rows.anchor: نظرة أي تأخير ، والنظرة الاسم من الأنظار ، وهو الإمهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has naẓira with a quiescent ẓāʾ; ʿAṭāʾ reads nāẓirahu, meaning the creditor waits or is the holder of the respite.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عطاء { * فناظره } أي فصاحب الحق أي منتظره

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: A further reading attributed to ʿAṭāʾ is an imperative: grant the debtor respite until ease.
rows.anchor: وعنه فناظره على الأمر أي فسامحه بالنظرة إلى الميسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysara derives from ease and wealth, the opposite of hardship; maysara, yusr, and maysūr all mean wealth.
rows.anchor: الميسرة مفعلة من اليسر واليسار ، الذي هو ضد الأعسار

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads maysara with a ḍamma on the sīn; the other readers use a fatḥa, the more common of the two dialect forms.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع { إلى ميسرة } بضم السين والباقون بفتحها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وشريح والضحاك والسدي وإبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Shurayḥ, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Suddī, and Ibrāhīm hold that the respite rule applies to usurious debts.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وشريح والضحاك والسدي وإبراهيم : الآية في الربا

rows.speaker: شريح
rows.claim: Shurayḥ reportedly ordered a debtor jailed despite a claim of insolvency, explaining that the respite rule concerns usury and citing the duty to return trusts.
rows.anchor: فقال شريح : إنما ذلك في الربا ، والله تعالى قال في كتابه

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators report that four brothers who had dealt in usury agreed to take only their principal after the threat of war, but Banu al-Mughira could not pay until the harvest and were refused delay; then this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: فشكا بنو المغيرة العسرة ، وقالوا : أخرونا إلى أن تدرك الغلات ، فأبوا أن يؤخروهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد وجماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: Mujāhid and a group of commentators apply the rule to all debts, arguing that the wording does not restrict hardship to the purchaser.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : وهو قول مجاهد وجماعة من المفسرين : إنها عامة في كل دين

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi says the context makes the usury-specific reading stronger because the preceding passage addresses usury and its threat of war.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أرجح ، لأنه تعالى قال في الآية المتقدمة

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi extends the duty to other debts by the shared reason that one unable to pay cannot be charged with payment; Razi says this is the majority jurists’ view, including Abu Hanifa, Malik, and al-Shafiʿi.
rows.anchor: ثبت وجوبه في سائر الصور ضرورة الاشتراك في المعنى ، وهو أن العاجز عن أداء المال لا يجوز تكليفه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A debtor is insolvent only if the estate has neither property available to pay the debt nor assets that could be sold to cover it.
rows.anchor: الإعسار هو أن لا يجد في ملكه ما يؤديه بعينه ، ولا يكون له ما لو باعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A debtor who owns a house or clothes is not insolvent if they can be sold to pay the debt, but may keep daily food and necessary clothes for prayer and protection from weather.
rows.anchor: من وحد دارا وثيابا لا يعد في ذوي العسرة ، إذا ما أمكنه بيعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists disagree whether an able-bodied insolvent debtor must hire out his labor to the creditor or another person to pay the debt.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا إذا كان قويا هل يلزمه أن يؤاجر نفسه من صاحب الدين أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists also disagree whether an insolvent debtor must accept another person’s offer to pay the debt on his behalf.
rows.anchor: إذا كان معسرا ، وقد بذل غيره ما يؤديه ، هل يلزمه القبول والأداء أو لا يلزمه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A debtor with goods that have become unsalable must sell them at a loss if necessary and apply the proceeds to the debt.
rows.anchor: فأما من له بضاعة كسدت عليه ، فواجب عليه أن يبيعها بالنقصان إن لم يكن إلا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowingly imprisoning a proven insolvent debtor or demanding payment is wrongful; the creditor must wait until the debtor becomes solvent.
rows.anchor: إذا علم الإنسان أن غريمه معسر جرم عليه حبسه ، وأن يطالبه بما له عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the creditor has reason to doubt the insolvency claim, detention is allowed until the debtor’s status becomes clear.
rows.anchor: فأما إن كانت له ريبة في إعساره فيجوز له أن يحبسه إلى وقت ظهور الإعسار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a debt arising from sale or loan, a debtor disputing insolvency must produce two upright witnesses that the received consideration was lost.
rows.anchor: وفي القسم الأول لا بد من إقامة شاهدين عدلين على أن ذلك العوض قد هلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a debt without consideration, such as damages, dowry, or guarantee, the debtor’s word is accepted and creditors must prove otherwise because poverty is the presumption.
rows.anchor: كان القول قوله وعلى الغرماء البينة لأن الأصل هو الفقر

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim reads tasaddaqu with a light ṣād; the other readers geminate it, reflecting deletion or assimilation of one of the original two tāʾs.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم { تصدقوا } بتخفيف الصاد والباقون بتشديدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that creditors forgive some or all of the debt owed by the insolvent; the omitted object is clear from the preceding mention of the debtor and principal.
rows.anchor: وأن تصدقوا على المعسر بما عليه من الدين إذ لا يصح التصدق به على غيره

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that whoever delays a Muslim’s due debt receives the reward of charity for each day of delay.
rows.anchor: لقوله عليه السلام ( لا يحل دين رجل مسلم فيؤخره إلا كان له بكل يوم صدقة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second interpretation takes charity to mean granting more time, but Razi rejects it because respite is already obligatory and ‘better for you’ fits a recommended act.
rows.anchor: هذا القول ضعيف ، لأن الإنظار ثبت وجوبه بالآية الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good promised by charity is honorable praise in this world and abundant reward in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: المراد بالخير حصول الثناء الجميل في الدنيا والثواب الجزيل في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of ‘if you know’ makes acting on the knowledge a condition, which serves as a severe warning to those who disobey.
rows.anchor: فجعل العمل من لوازم العلم ، وفيه تهديد شديد على العصاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading means if you know that charity is better than granting respite and collecting the debt.
rows.anchor: إن كنتم تعلمون فضل التصدق على الإنظار والقبض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading means if you know that what your Lord commands is more beneficial for you.
rows.anchor: إن كنتم تعلمون أن ما يأمركم به ربكم أصلح لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning addresses wealthy, powerful usurers who could dominate others; they needed a stronger threat to stop usury and wrongful seizure of people’s property.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الآية في العظماء الذين كانوا يعاملون بالربا وكانوا أصحاب ثروة وجلال وأنصار وأعوان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this was the last verse revealed: after the verse on inheritance at 4:127 and the verse revealed at ʿArafah at 5:3, Gabriel ordered it placed at the end of al-Baqarah; reports give the Prophet’s remaining lifetime as eighty-one, twenty-one, seven days, or three hours.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هذه الآية آخر أية نزلت على الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads tarjiʿūn with an open tāʾ while the others use a ḍamma; the readings follow the distinction between intransitive rajaʿa and transitive rajjaʿa.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو { ترجعون } بفتح التاء والباقون بضم التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawman is an accusative direct object, not a time adverb: people must prepare to meet that day through good works, as in the warning at 73:17.
rows.anchor: لا على الظرف ، لأنه ليس المعنى : واتقوا في هذا اليوم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi says the day itself is not what can be avoided; its horrors are avoided in worldly life by refraining from sins and fulfilling duties, so the command encompasses all legal obligations.
rows.anchor: واتقاء تلك الأهوال لا يمكن إلا في دار الدنيا بمجانبة المعاصي الواجبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning to God cannot mean spatial movement or returning to His knowledge, since God is beyond place and already with people wherever they are.
rows.anchor: المراد منه ما يتعلق بالمكان والجهة فإن ذلك محال على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sound interpretation of return to God is that after death people return to the state before worldly life, when God alone visibly directs their affairs; parents and others direct them outwardly after birth.
rows.anchor: فكأنه بعد الخروج عن الدنيا عاد إلى الحالة التي كان عليها قبل الدخول في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second sound interpretation is that people return to the reward or punishment God has prepared for them.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد يرجعون إلى ما أعد الله لهم من ثواب أو عقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every accountable person receives the full recompense for deeds, as shown by the smallest deed being seen and by the just scales; Razi also cites the mustard seed hidden in rock, heaven, or earth.
rows.anchor: كل مكلف فهو عند الرجوع إلى الله لا بد وأن يصل إليه جزاء عمله بالتمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘What it earned’ can mean the recompense for its deeds, with an omitted word, or the recompense itself as what the person acquired; Razi prefers the latter because it avoids ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وهذا التأويل أولى ، لأنه مهما أمكن تفسير الكلام

rows.speaker: الوعيدية
rows.claim: The proponents of the threat doctrine use the verse to establish with certainty that grave sinners will face punishment.
rows.anchor: الوعيدية يتمسكون بهذه الآية على القطع بوعيد الفساق

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi’s theologians use the verse to establish that believers will not remain eternally in Hell: they must receive faith’s reward, which requires leaving the Fire for Paradise.
rows.anchor: ولا يمكن ذلك إلا بأن يخرج من النار ويدخل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi asks why ‘they are not wronged’ is added after full recompense, then answers that full recompense entails punishment and the phrase answers the objection that punishing servants conflicts with divine generosity.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك دليلا على إيصال العذاب إلى الفساق والكفار ، فكان لقائل أن يقول : كيف يليق بكرم أكرم الأكرمين

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilite answer is that people bring ruin on themselves because God enables them, removes their excuses, makes reasoning accessible, and gives them time; Razi says this answer works only on Muʿtazilite premises.
rows.anchor: وهذا الجواب إنما يستقيم على أصول المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the theologians’ premises, God owns creation and may act in His property as He wills without injustice, which is what ‘they are not wronged’ indicates after the threat.
rows.anchor: هو أنه سبحانه مالك الخلق ، والمالك إذا تصرف في ملكه كيف شاء وأراد لم يكن ظلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi identifies the debt-document verse as the third legal ruling discussed in this passage of the surah.
rows.anchor: من الأحكام الشرعية المذكورة في هذا الموضع من هذه السورة آية المداينة

none: The segment contains only a slash, so its source text is broken or missing.

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators restrict the preceding general statement to Christians because of its occasion of revelation.
rows.anchor: بعض المفسرين خصص ذلك بالنصارى ، فقصر اللفظ العام على سبب نزوله

rows.speaker: المحققون من المفسرين
rows.claim: The more rigorous exegetes hold that a specific occasion does not restrict general wording, so the statement covers everyone who turns away from God’s signs.
rows.anchor: خصوص السبب لا يمنع عموم اللفظ ، فهو يتناول كل من أعرض عن دلائل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is the unconquerable victor, while al-Intiqām means punishment; al-Layth explains the verb as requiting someone for what they did.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث يقال : لم أرض عنه حتى نقمت منه وانتقمت إذا كافأه عقوب بما صنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi identifies al-ʿAzīz as an attribute of essence, indicating power to punish, and dhū intiqām as an attribute of action, indicating that God performs punishment.
rows.anchor: فالأول : صفة الذات ، والثاني : صفة الفعل
